title: 凤凰台上忆吹箫·香冷金猊
title_en: Remembering the Flute on Phoenix Terrace: The Incense Is Cold
author: 李清照

text_note.zh: 语料库是另一个版本，有多处不同：“起来慵自梳头”作“起来人未梳头”，“任宝奁尘满”作“任宝奁闲掩”，“生怕离怀别苦”作“生怕闲愁暗恨”，“新来瘦”作“今年瘦”，“休休”作“明朝”，“也则难留”作“也即难留”，“念武陵人远，烟锁秦楼”作“念武陵春晚，云锁重楼”，“惟有楼前流水”作“记取楼前绿水”，“从今又添，一段新愁”作“从今更数，几段新愁”。这里用常见选本的文字。
text_note.en: The corpus has a different version of this lyric, with many changes. For example, it has "I have not yet combed my hair" for "I cannot bother to comb my hair", "this year I am thin" for "lately I am thin", "tomorrow morning" for "enough, let it go", "spring is late in Wuling, clouds lock the many-storeyed tower" for "the man of Wuling is far, mist locks the Qin tower", and "from now I will count how many new sorrows" for "from now one more new sorrow". Here we use the text in common anthologies.

readings.zh: 欲说还休的“还”，现在一般读 hái，意思是“又、却”。也有人读 huán。
readings.en: In yù shuō hái xiū it is usually read hái, "and yet". Some read it huán.

readings.zh: 非干的“干”读 gān，意思是“关系到”，不读 gàn。
readings.en: In fēi gān it is read gān, "to concern", not gàn.

glosses.zh: 金猊：狮子形状的铜香炉。猊，狻猊，传说中像狮子的猛兽。
glosses.en: jīn ní: a bronze incense burner shaped like a lion. Ní is a lion-like beast from old stories.

glosses.zh: 被翻红浪：红色的被子乱摊在床上，像翻起的红色波浪。
glosses.en: bèi fān hóng làng: the red quilt lies tossed on the bed like rolling red waves.

glosses.zh: 慵：懒，没有精神。
glosses.en: yōng: lazy, without spirit.

glosses.zh: 任：任凭，随它去。
glosses.en: rèn: to let it be.

glosses.zh: 宝奁：精美的梳妆盒。
glosses.en: bǎo lián: a fine box for combs and make-up.

glosses.zh: 日上帘钩：太阳升到挂帘子的钩子那么高了，就是说时间已经不早。
glosses.en: rì shàng lián gōu: the sun has climbed as high as the curtain hook, so it is already late in the morning.

glosses.zh: 生怕：最怕，非常怕。
glosses.en: shēng pà: to fear most of all.

glosses.zh: 离怀别苦：离别的愁思和痛苦。
glosses.en: lí huái bié kǔ: the sorrow and pain of parting.

glosses.zh: 欲说还休：想说又停住不说了。
glosses.en: yù shuō hái xiū: wanting to speak, but stopping.

glosses.zh: 新来：近来。
glosses.en: xīn lái: lately.

glosses.zh: 非干病酒：不是因为喝酒喝病了。非干，不关。
glosses.en: fēi gān bìng jiǔ: it is not because wine has made her ill.

glosses.zh: 悲秋：因为秋天到了而伤心。
glosses.en: bēi qiū: feeling sad because autumn has come.

glosses.zh: 休休：算了吧，罢了。
glosses.en: xiū xiū: enough, let it go.

glosses.zh: 这回去也：这一次离开呀。
glosses.en: zhè huí qù yě: this time, he is going away.

glosses.zh: 阳关：指《阳关曲》，是根据王维的送别诗谱成的送别歌。唱千万遍，是说送别的歌唱了无数遍。
glosses.en: yáng guān: the Song of Yangguan, a farewell song set to Wang Wei's parting poem. Singing it ten thousand times means singing it over and over.

glosses.zh: 也则难留：也还是留不住。
glosses.en: yě zé nán liú: still he cannot be kept.

glosses.zh: 武陵人远：武陵人，用古代传说里进入仙境的人，代指远行的丈夫。人远，人已经走远了。
glosses.en: wǔ líng rén yuǎn: the man of Wuling, from an old story of someone who wandered into a land of immortals. It stands for her husband, now far away.

glosses.zh: 烟锁秦楼：烟雾笼罩着秦楼。秦楼，传说中秦穆公的女儿弄玉和丈夫萧史吹箫住的楼，这里指自己住的楼。
glosses.en: yān suǒ qín lóu: mist locks in the Qin tower. In legend this was where Nongyu, daughter of Duke Mu of Qin, lived and played the flute with her husband Xiao Shi. Here it means her own room.

glosses.zh: 凝眸：目不转睛地看，一直盯着看。
glosses.en: níng móu: to gaze fixedly, without looking away.

glosses.zh: 又添：又增加了。
glosses.en: yòu tiān: adds once more.

translation.zh: 狮子香炉里的香已经冷了，
translation.en: The incense in the lion-shaped burner has gone cold.

translation.zh: 红被子乱摊着像翻起的波浪，
translation.en: The red quilt lies tossed like rolling waves.
I get up and cannot bother to comb my hair.
I let the make-up box gather dust,

translation.zh: 太阳已经升到了帘钩那么高。
translation.en: while the sun climbs as high as the curtain hook.
What I fear most is the pain of parting.
So many things are on my mind,
I want to say them, then stop.
Lately I have grown thin,
not because wine has made me ill,

translation.zh: 也不是因为秋天让人伤心。
translation.en: and not because autumn makes me sad.
Enough, let it go!
This time he is going.

translation.zh: 就算把送别的歌唱上千万遍，
translation.en: Even if we sang the farewell song ten thousand times,
he still could not be kept.

translation.zh: 想到远行的人已经走远，
translation.en: I think of him, gone far away,
while mist closes round my tower.
Only the stream in front of the tower
must remember me,
gazing out all day long.
There where I gaze,
from today on there will be
one more new sorrow.

background.zh: 这首词写的是丈夫赵明诚要出远门，李清照在家中送别时的愁苦。一般认为是她和丈夫分别前后写的，但具体是哪一年，说法不一。词牌“凤凰台上忆吹箫”来自一个传说：秦穆公的女儿弄玉和丈夫萧史都爱吹箫，后来一起乘着凤凰飞走了。这个词牌很适合写夫妻离别。
background.en: This lyric is about the sorrow Li Qingzhao felt at home when her husband Zhao Mingcheng was setting off on a long journey. It is usually thought to have been written around the time they parted, but sources disagree on the year. The tune name comes from a legend. Nongyu, daughter of Duke Mu of Qin, and her husband Xiao Shi both loved to play the flute, and in the end they flew away together on phoenixes. So the tune suits a lyric about a husband and wife apart.

author_note.zh: 李清照（1084—约1155），号易安居士，宋代最有名的女词人。她和丈夫赵明诚感情很好，两人一起收藏金石书画。她前期的词多写闺中生活和离别相思，语言浅白又细腻，是婉约词的代表。
author_note.en: Li Qingzhao (1084 to about 1155), also called Yi'an, was the most famous woman poet of the Song. She and her husband Zhao Mingcheng loved each other deeply and collected old bronzes, stone rubbings, books and paintings together. Her early lyrics are mostly about life at home and missing someone far away. Her words are plain yet delicate, a model of the gentle style.

appreciation.zh: 这首词写离别，却几乎不直接说“我很难过”。开头只写一个早晨：香炉冷了，被子乱着，人起来了却懒得梳头，梳妆盒积了灰，太阳都老高了。这些小事一摆出来，就能看出她没心思做任何事。她说有很多话想说又说不出口；人瘦了，却不是因为喝酒，也不是因为秋天。没说出的原因，读者一看就懂：是因为丈夫要走。下阕一声“休休”，像叹了一口长气：唱多少遍送别歌也留不住他。人走远了，楼被烟雾锁住，只有楼前的流水陪她整天张望。最后说望的地方又多了一段新愁，把思念写得又细又长。
appreciation.en: This lyric is about parting, yet it almost never says "I am sad" outright. It begins with one morning: the incense burner is cold, the quilt is tossed, she gets up but cannot bother to comb her hair, the make-up box gathers dust, and the sun is already high. These small things show that she has no heart for anything. She says she has much to say but cannot say it. She has grown thin, but not from wine and not from autumn. She leaves the real reason unsaid, and the reader understands at once: her husband is leaving. The second stanza opens with "enough, enough", like a long sigh. No number of farewell songs can keep him. He is far away now, mist locks in her tower, and only the stream below keeps her company as she gazes out all day. At the end she says the place where she gazes now holds one more new sorrow. Her longing is drawn out thin and long.
